newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Sept 17.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Leading shares again shied away from the 4,000 level in London in another day of patchy trading and as Wall Street failed to provide impetus for another push forward, traders said on Tuesday. Any hopes of a lift from New York in the afternoon quickly evaporated after reports that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System had requested a rise in interest rates amid evidence of brisk economic growth. The index finished with a loss of 4.9 points at 3,972.3.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade flat on Tuesday after the rallies seen in the last two trading days began to wane and dealers said there was now the possibility of a small correction in stock values. The DAX index of 30 blue chip German shares closed 1.79 points down at 2,628.08 on volumes described by dealers as particularly thin. In post-bourse trade the index fell 3.81 to 2,626.43.

PARIS - French shares closed lower on Tuesday reversing their gains in late trade as rate hike fears in the United States drove Wall Street lower, dealers said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.33 points at 2,080.86.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a weak day markedly lower on moderate volumes after Wall Street opening losses led to a late slide on the Swiss bourse, dealers said. Dealers were disappointed with the market's fall below 3,700 SMI points. "Presently, Zurich only follows negative moves on Wall Street, not the positive ones", a dealer said. Trade was dominated by professional and the price moves are expected to remain volatile throughout the week. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 17.22 points to 2,366.78 points.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's benchmark Nikkei 225 average galloped higher in late afternoon trade on Tuesday to close 467.95 points higher at 21,310.59.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended firmer on Tuesday and the Hang Seng index hit its highest close since February 1994, buoyed by Wall Street's highs and the view that a near-term rate hike would not hit stocks hard, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index closed up 53.71 points at 11,621.61, off a peak of 11,645.35.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market was dragged to a lower close on Tuesday by a weak resource sector, which was hit by lower metal prices and ignored the record high hit on Wall Street on Monday. The All Ordinaries index was 13.4 points down at 2,254.4, just off the low of 2,252.9. The fall almost wiped out the previous day's 15.5 point gain.
JOHANNESBURG - The Johannesburg Stock Exchange was on Tuesday awash with positive sentiment, heaving South African industrial and gold shares to a strong finish.

Dealers said a batch of upbeat factors, including record gains on world markets and a steady rand, were responsible for the confident mood. Continued futures-related basket trading, mainly on the March 1997 contract but also on the December 1996 contract, supported firmness. Traders said overall market strength was seen continuing on Wednesday unless Wall Street came in for a pounding. The industrial index finished 26.2 points better at 8,211.7 elevating the overall index to 6,947.1, 20.8 points up. The gold index ended 25.2 points firmer at 1,776.5.
